title: Autonomous roving canary with session consistency and playback support
author: Marina Delgado
description: Context: We need safer canary strategies for stateful LLM sessions (chat-like flows) where splitting by user ID can still surface regressions tied to session affinity or state. Current canaries either shadow (no user-visible change) or static canary cohorts that remain pinned to a subset of traffic, which delays discovery of issues that only appear when canary runs across many different session histories. This PR introduces an autonomous 'roving canary' controller that incrementally and deterministically moves canary assignment across session shards while preserving session consistency for active sessions. It also adds a lightweight replay/playback hook that captures minimal session context for deterministic repro on the canary model when a telemetry alert fires. Motivation: reduce time-to-detect for regressions that only manifest across varied session histories; enable post-failure deterministic playback for faster RCA. What changed (high level): 1) New roving controller that implements timebox-driven shard rotation and ensures in-flight sessions remain pinned until completion; 2) Session-affinity table and graceful handoff code to avoid mid-session model flips; 3) Deterministic playback library that captures nonce-limited KV cache and prompt slices for safe replay in a sandboxed execution path; 4) Console UI hooks and rollout graphing to visualize roving sweep progress; 5) E2E tests and loadbench scenarios for mixed session-length distributions. Rollout plan: staged merge to main, enable behind feature flag rollout.roving_canary=false by default, smoke rollout to internal org with 1% of traffic, then enable 5%, 20% progressing via automatic health gates. On alert, controller automatically pauses and schedules playback jobs for recent sessions from the roving windows. Backwards compatibility: controller degrades to static cohort assignment if the session-affinity store is unavailable. Safety: we enforce a max-sessions-in-flight threshold and a kill-switch that immediately collapses roving back into stable cohort. Related work: builds on ENG-2029 (canary orchestration) and ENG-2058 (session affinity API). Checklist: - [x] Controller implementation + unit tests - [x] Playback capture library + sandboxed runner - [x] Console visualization and metrics - [x] Loadbench scenarios - [x] Documentation and runbook entries - [x] Feature flag gated and documented Known limitations: playback currently supports only deterministic prefix capture (no external tool integrations yet); migration path for very long-lived sessions requires reconfiguration of the max-inflight window. Release notes: see field below.

review_conversation: Aaron Patel (2026-02-12): Can you elaborate on the security model for saved playback artifacts? Response: Playback artifacts are nonce-signed, encrypted at rest with customer KMS in Private deployments; in hosted, artifacts live in a short-lived encryption key and auto-expire after 72 hours.

Sophie Nguyen (2026-02-13): I'm concerned about mid-session latency spikes when reassigning shards. Response: We added a in-flight session threshold and handoff path so active sessions are never moved until completion; rotation only affects new sessions post-tick.

Kofi Mensah (2026-02-15): Tests look good, but add a regression test for long-lived sessions. Author reply (2026-02-16): Added a long-lived session e2e case and a soak job in loadbench, see tests/e2e/roving_sweep_spec.go.
Aaron Patel (2026-02-18): Approving after a minor comment on log verbosity. Author: reduced debug logs and added feature flag gating for verbose traces.
release_notes: Feature: Autonomous 'roving canary' rollout controller for session-aware canaries; Feature: Deterministic session playback for fast RCA. Notes: Feature is behind rollout.roving_canary flag and disabled by default. Admins should read docs/runbooks/roving_canary.md before enabling; playback artifacts expire automatically and are encrypted in hosted runs.
merge_outcome: Merged into main via squash on 2026-02-20. Post-merge: feature flag default=false. Manual canary experiment scheduled for 2026-02-25 internal org.
post_merge_actions: Enable feature flag in staging and run loadbench sweep
Schedule a 1% internal org canary and monitor roving.sweep_success and roving.playback_failures metrics
Follow runbook steps for playback retrieval and sandboxed replay
notes: This PR intentionally keeps playback capture minimal to avoid PII leakage; engineering and security reviewed the artifact schema. The roving controller is pluggable and can be toggled to use static cohorts for customers that prefer deterministic traffic splits.
